findings: ExecuteDestroyed previously published destruction history synchronously during generation. Client action/autoplay generation precedes local DoSubActions, whose five receivers have six gated history sites.
Attack double-death history is attacker first, then defender. Generation destruction effects are defender first, then attacker; moving publication avoids reversing effects or running them twice.

Explicit batch destroy history follows its pruned cardsToDestroy notification. Batch damage history follows aligned damageReceiverIDs/destroyed flags, even when later callbacks prune physical death processing.

Batch damage early victory returns can skip destruction callbacks/output IDs after its damage notification has already captured death flags; receipt history cannot be inferred from that final output list.
changes: Queue destruction-history work from the five emitted notification names. Preserve ID order and duplicate occurrences, and honor per-entry or role death flags.
Drain using current object CardID/Owner and current State.Turn. Use UpdateDestroyedCardsIDs only; retain its duplicate global/per-side and unique per-turn behavior.
Remove immediate history write from ExecuteDestroyed, preserving generation effects and UnitDestroyedThisTurn. Receipt processing emits no additional subactions and does not reset this flag.
Use the existing local receipt queue alongside Gotcha/frontline/end-turn entries. Existing high-level drain points remain; standalone callers explicitly drain.

Add three headless tests covering 48 scenarios; update 21 previous fixtures to explicit receipt boundaries and correct notification-driven expected histories. The after-defense callback asserts history is still empty; no automatic flush added inside callbacks.
validation: Fresh 11 whole runtime Blueprint bodies: 34116 bytes, 1142 decoded statements; script/header/FName/symbol/hash/executable guards verified. Five receiver bodies exactly match the independently modeled RULE-393 capture.

Reran 576 controlled local=true PvP receiver AST models and 1024 history models with 15360 count queries. Their controlled native/container/delegate primitives do not certify actual engine scheduling.

New tests against old kernel: 3/823 fail. After production patch all three pass but 21 older synchronous-history fixtures fail; after reviewed receipt-boundary updates Release selftest passes 823/823.

DeepSeek extracted 21 failing-method source contexts in a private packet. All returned method/line/text coordinates independently checked against its source snapshot. Primary chose all semantic changes and owns integration/publishing.
limits: Only the destruction-history publication portion of valid retained-object local receipts is integrated. DestroyedCountChanged and daily notifier callbacks are not dispatched by this adapter; no full receiver equivalence claim.

Native remote physical-mutation branches, null/default context behavior, released/replaced objects, GC and arbitrary callback reentry remain uncertified. Missing headless lookups are skipped; this is not certified as native null behavior.

Attack history holds the selected dead-role references at receipt entry. Native receivers hold both roles before their additional notifications. Since those notifications are not integrated here, transitive callback/lifetime equivalence remains open.
The existing local queue models selected rule-bearing receipts, not all ResolveSubAction/DoSubActions behavior or nested shared-local-mode overwrite semantics.
Owner and turn mutations in new tests are controlled dataflow probes, not claims that the captured live match produced those transitions.
Standalone rule APIs require an explicit ApplyPendingLocalRuleReceipts boundary. Normal high-level actions already drain after generation/autoplay. Future callers must preserve this contract.
Single-card version migration remains paused; fully certified cards remains 0. Historical replays were not used as authority.
